title: The GA4 export against the backend, by first touch

brief.decision: Whether the 2026 growth report can read sign-ups and first payments per first-touch source and medium from the GA4 export instead of the backend
brief.deadline: Declan's growth review in the second week of January 2026

expected_output.grain: one row per first-touch source and medium with at least one sign-up or first payment on the Dublin days of Q4 2025, on either side

checkpoints.prompt: Declan asks how many sign-ups each first-touch source and medium brought in on the Dublin days from 1 October to 31 December 2025, read from the GA4 export alone. In events, event_date holds that Dublin day as text, traffic_source holds the visitor's first touch, and a visitor who denied consent sends events with no user_pseudo_id or user_id; those sign-ups count too. Before you write any SQL, which rows of events, counted how, answer that?

options.text: The sign_up events with an event_date from '20251001' to '20251231' and a user_pseudo_id, each counted once, grouped by the source and medium in traffic_source.
The different user_pseudo_id values among the sign_up events with an event_date from '20251001' to '20251231', grouped by the source and medium in traffic_source.
The sign_up events with an event_date from '20251001' to '20251231', each counted once, grouped by the source and medium in traffic_source.
The sign_up events with an event_date from '20251001' to '20251231', each counted once, grouped by the utm_source and utm_medium of the session their ga_session_id points to.

checkpoints.prompt: Declan first wants the size of the export's side. How many sign-ups does the GA4 export record over the Dublin days from 1 October to 31 December 2025? A sign-up is a sign_up event, and event_date holds its Dublin day. Count each such event once, including those with no user_pseudo_id, from visitors who denied consent, and those Mailvora's server sends. Type a whole number.
Write the query that answers Declan's question.

Declan's headline: take the subscriptions whose first payment, the earliest paid_at among the subscription's payments, fell on a Dublin day from 1 October to 31 December 2025, that is from 2025-09-30 23:00:00 UTC up to but not including 2026-01-01 00:00:00 UTC; a first payment that was later refunded counts. In the GA4 export each of them is one purchase event, dated by event_date, with the paying visitor's first touch in traffic_source. What percentage of them came from a visitor whose first-touch medium is a paid one: cpc, paid_social, video or affiliate? Type the percentage rounded to 1 decimal, for example 12.3.

Declan's result counts every sign_up and purchase event, the sign_ups with no user_pseudo_id from visitors who denied consent included, and it counts a first payment that was later refunded on both sides, as the export keeps its purchase and has no refund event. It shows the export's sign-ups and first payments equal to the backend's in every first-touch source and medium over the Dublin days of Q4 2025, and the export holds each visitor's first touch only, in traffic_source. What can Declan conclude from this result?

options.text: The export also holds each session's own source and medium, so a last-touch report read from the export would match the backend just as well.
The sources with the most first payments caused those payments, so the 2026 budget can follow these counts from one source to the next.
The export can stand in for the backend on these first-touch counts, but its purchases still include first payments refunded later.
The export leaves out the visitors who denied consent, so the counts match only because the backend leaves the same visitors out as well.

checkpoints.prompt: Write 2 to 4 sentences for Declan: whether the export can feed the growth report, the headline number, one caveat and one next step.

model_plan:
Metric formula: ga4_signups and ga4_first_payments, the sign_up and purchase events of a first-touch source and medium; backend_signups and backend_first_payments, the signups and the subscriptions' first payments of the visitors whose first session had that source and medium; 0 where there are none.
Output grain: one row per first-touch source and medium with a sign-up or a first payment on either side.
Tables and keys: events alone for the export, read through traffic_source; payments down to each subscription's earliest paid_at, joined to subscriptions on subscription_id and to signups on user_id for the visitor; sessions down to each visitor's earliest session_start, joined on visitor_id; the two sides joined on source and medium.
Filters: event_date from 20251001 to 20251231; signup_ts and the first paid_at on the same Dublin days, each turned from a UTC instant into Europe/Dublin time first.
Edge cases: a sign_up with no user_pseudo_id, from a visitor who denied consent, still counts; every purchase comes from the server and counts; a first payment refunded later counts on both sides; a missing UTM value reads as (direct) or (none); a visitor's first session can come before October.
Expected row count: 34
model_answer_template: Over the Dublin days of Q4 2025 the GA4 export's {CP2} sign-ups and its first payments matched the backend in every first-touch source and medium, so the growth report can read them from the export. {CP4} percent of the quarter's first payments came from visitors whose first touch was a paid medium, a share the report can now follow from the export alone. The match holds for each visitor's first touch with the consent-denied events counted, and the export still counts a first payment refunded later as a purchase, so net paying customers need the backend's refund flag. Next, flag refunded purchases by joining transaction_id to payments, and rerun this check each month.
follow_up_question: Which first-touch sources had the highest share of refunded first payments in Q4 2025?
